name: browserwright-search
label: Google via your Chrome
_note: kind: "module" rather than "command" because a search is a lifecycle, not
one shot at a subprocess: mint a session, navigate, extract, retry once on an
executor death, tear down in a finally. See the header of the .ts runner for
the six measured executor behaviours it is designed around.
timeoutMs is 120s, well above the measured cost. Google through a real
browser took 10-21s warm on 2026-08-09 (page.goto's own settle wait accounts
for ~2.5s of that; the rest is Google's page never going network-quiet).
Slow is accepted here — this rung exists for correctness and login state, not
for throughput.
failWhen.matches is [] because the extraction returns rows, not prose: the
default needles ('captcha', 'just a moment') would be matched against result
titles and snippets, where they appear legitimately in any query about them.
The runner detects real interstitials from the page HTML instead and reports
them as a reason.
minResults 1 is the real guard. A captcha or consent wall parses perfectly
and yields an empty list, which is the failure mode that would otherwise be
indistinguishable from an honestly empty search.
searchUrl is a template so the engine can be swapped without touching code.
{queryEncoded} and {limit} are the only substitutions.
SERP features (measured 2026-08-10, see docs/adr/0008). The page is server-
rendered for organic rows, but the AI Overview body is NOT in the initial HTML
at all — it streams in afterwards. That is why extraction runs against the
live DOM and not the document response. browserwright's page.goto already
waits long enough: both organic and the AI Overview were present 0.02s after
it returned.
Each extractor is independently guarded, because the realistic failure is one
restyled container taking the whole search down with it. Anchors used, worst
to best: AI Overview has no stable hook at all, so it anchors on the
accessible heading and walks up; the knowledge panel uses data-attrid, which
is semantic markup rather than a styling class and is the sturdiest hook on
the page; PAA uses data-q (which also carries the query itself, so that is
filtered); related searches are scoped to #botstuff because the same href
pattern at the top of the page is Google's own tab bar.
Known noise that is cleaned: snippets end with the 'Read more' expander text,
dates are prefixed onto snippets with either an em dash or a middot, the AI
Overview splices citation counters ('+2') into its prose, and pagination
renders 'Next' through the related-searches selector.
